questions.question: the largest recovered surface here spans 12 records of tile 160. Only 31% of the map's records sit in a shared projection at all. Should the writer keep projecting one frame per RUN, or per FLAT FACE? Measured over the 43 campaign maps the answer is the run: 93.7% of collinear solid-solid joins continue, 67.9% of bends and 19.1% of reflex corners.
questions.recommended_default: keep the run, and add nothing: RUN_BREAK_DEGREES already stops at 100 degrees, and the reader's census is the evidence for whether a bend break belongs in the writer too. Decide it on the whole campaign, which is now measured: see reports/campaign-census-2026-09-03.md

questions.question: 2481 records, 1075 of them with no same-material neighbour at all. Is a lone record a SURFACE of one, or is it evidence that our surface model does not fit how Blood was authored?
questions.recommended_default: count it as residue, as here: a frame fitted to one record reproduces it for free, and calling that understanding is how a coverage report reaches 100%
